source_text: Theologically, adherents in progressive Jewish circles reinterpret the Abrahamic covenant as achievable through symbolic affirmation of life and community inclusion rather than physical alteration, framing Brit Shalom as a "covenant of peace" that honors Jewish heritage without mandating excision, a view supported by rabbis in Reform and Reconstructionist traditions who facilitate such ceremonies to affirm parental autonomy. [20]
